message:
release: 0.2.152 -- security: the host takes session control only from the client it admitted

PC only. Security fix (udp-control-peer, t-2ydcedko; found by the verifier's call-chain trace, Codex P1):
the host handed every UDP control datagram (ControlData/Ack/Nack) to the session's control channel without
looking at who sent it, so another endpoint on the network could, as far as the source shows, inject
input/control into an authenticated session or forge ACK/NACK. Now the host's UDP reader compares each
datagram's address family + IP + port with the peer the session adopted (changed only by a Hello that passed
admission); control, video-NACK and bulk from any other endpoint are dropped before the parser with no state
change and no reply. No wire change. Clients already use connected UDP.
Verified: Codex OK on 7df9f24; verifier's independent build -- security e2e 94/0 x2 with a real-ingress
negative control (same commit with the check reverted: 10 FAIL, exit 1 -- injected command processed, old
endpoint not refused after a port move, a spoofed ACK matched to real outstanding data stops the
retransmit), control_resume 60/0; main integration 12 tests exit 0 (paste e2e with 0.2.150 binaries).
Not verified (stated, not passed): another source IP reaching the socket, video-NACK positive path, WAN
direct<->relay switch. This is not cryptographic authentication -- spoofed source addresses and on-path
attackers remain (separate transport-security design).

Product: version only (PC 0.2.151 -> 0.2.152; APK stays 0.2.26). Test: none. Docs: none.
